🔥🇲🇽 <u>47 OFFICIALS AND ONE COMPANY SANCTIONED IN MEXICO'S ANTI-CORRUPTION SWEEP</u>

Mexico's Anti-Corruption and Good Governance Secretariat sanctioned 47 public servants and one company — dismissals, bans of up to 10 years and 4.6 million pesos in fines. Among them: a CFE worker in Puebla banned for 10 years over nine fake medical certificates; an official at the Durango military hospital fined 651,000 pesos for supply and gas payments he couldn't account for; and a company fined 3.1 million pesos and barred for four years for submitting altered vehicle invoices in a public tender.

🇲🇽🇵🇸 <u>MEXICO JOINS THE HAGUE GROUP TO DEFEND INTERNATIONAL COURTS AND PALESTINE</u>

At UN headquarters, Mexico sat with some 40 nations convened by South Africa and Malaysia to defend the International Criminal Court, the International Court of Justice and the Palestinian people — after days of attacks and threats against those courts from Washington, Israel and their right-wing allies. Mexico, Brazil, Cuba and Norway joined the Hague Group. Mexico's alternate UN representative, Porfirio Thierry Muñoz Ledo: "We have to ensure and improve compliance and implementation of international law."

🇲🇽🤝 <u>1.6 MILLION PEOPLE IN GUERRERO NOW RECEIVE WELFARE PROGRAMS</u>

In Acapulco — battered by two hurricanes in 2023 and 2024 — President Sheinbaum reported that federal Bienestar programs now reach 1,637,427 people in Guerrero, alongside road, health, education and urban works across the state. "Education is the best vaccine against insecurity and crime," she said. "Nothing above those who have the least, nothing above the people — Guerrero will always be with the transformation."

🇲🇽🏭 <u>672,000 formal jobs in a single month</u>

Formal employment in Mexico grew by 672,313 positions in August, the biggest monthly gain of 2026 and the end of a three-month slide, per INEGI data reported by El Economista. Informal work fell by 734,097 and informality dropped 1.2 points to 55%. Unemployment ticked up to 3%, still one of the lowest rates in the OECD.

🚨🇲🇽 <u>Juchitán mayor arrested for extortion; Oaxaca dissolves local powers</u>

Miguel Sánchez Altamirano, mayor of Juchitán, Oaxaca, was arrested on September 23 for aggravated extortion and crimes against state security. Prosecutors link him to "Los Cromos," a CJNG cell. Navy, Defense, SSPC, National Guard and FGR joined the operation under Sheinbaum's "Zero Impunity" policy. It came days after gunmen attacked the home of muxe designer Elvis Guerra, who had reported extortion threats, though Sheinbaum says the arrest isn't tied to that attack. Oaxaca's Congress has now approved dissolving the municipality's powers.

🇲🇽🛢️ <u>59-million-liter fuel case: FGR's Guanajuato delegate fired</u>

Juan Francisco Vera, the FGR delegate in Guanajuato, has been removed over irregularities in the seizure of the fuel plant where more than 59 million liters were secured. García Harfuch said the site was reported two weeks after the seizure, on September 17, and the documents on the fuel's origin were never verified. The case now goes to FEMDO, the organized-crime unit, which will determine whether the Grupo SIMSA–Gas Natural del Noroeste companies had valid permits and traceable fuel.

🇲🇽🍫 <u>Tabasco cacao: 16,771 small farmers, 10,000 tons</u>

Tabasco expects to produce 10,000 metric tons of cacao in the cycle starting November–December, from 16,771 small producers on 23,949 hectares, 63% of it ejido land. Alimentación para el Bienestar has already bought 524 tons from 3,223 farmers with 114 million pesos, and a 126-million-peso chocolate plant in Comalcalco is due in 2027. The crop Mesoamerica gave the world, now processed at home.

🇲🇽🏥 <u>Chiapas gets a 120-bed cancer and blood disease center</u>

Chiapas, Mexico's poorest state, will build a State Hemato-Oncology Center in Tuxtla Gutiérrez with 120 beds, 26 specialty consulting rooms and a transplant unit, a joint project with IMSS-Bienestar. Patients with leukemia and cancer from across the south will no longer have to travel to other states for specialized treatment.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>PAN's Benito Juárez under investigation: 48 properties flagged</u>

Mexico City's Comptroller has opened a case against the PAN-run Benito Juárez borough, headed by Luis Mendoza, for possible construction and land-use violations on 48 properties. It stems from the "real estate cartel": borough officials in Public Works, Legal and Government who authorized more floors than allowed so private developers could sell overpriced apartments, fueling gentrification and speculation. PAN has governed Benito Juárez without interruption since 2000.

🇲🇽📊 <u>INFLATION TICKS UP TO 3.42%, CORE KEEPS COOLING</u>

Mexico’s annual inflation rose to 3.42% in the first half of September from 3.26%, Inegi reported — pushed by tomatoes, up 22.79% in just two weeks. But core inflation, which strips out volatile prices, eased to 3.79% from 3.83%, and the headline stays inside Banxico’s 3% ±1 target band. Services remain the sticky part at 4.33%, per El Economista.
